evidence.item: OpenAI told Reuters that its annualized revenue run rate reached $10 billion as of June, up from approximately $5.5 billion in December 2024.
evidence.shows: The threshold was reported for OpenAI itself by June; the figure excluded Microsoft licensing revenue and large one-time deals.

evidence.item: Epoch AI compiled reported OpenAI run rates of $2 billion at the end of 2023, $5.5 billion at the end of 2024 and $10 billion on June 9, 2025; it estimated growth of about 3.2 times per year over the longer period through August 2025.
evidence.shows: The rapid growth trend broadly continued, though more slowly than a precise doubling every six months.

evidence.item: OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar reported annualized revenue of approximately $2 billion in 2023, $6 billion in 2024 and over $20 billion in 2025.
evidence.shows: A company statement independently supports the approximate year-end figures and continued rapid growth; it does not identify the first month in which the run rate reached $10 billion.

SA-046.thesis: A big tech company could plausibly reach an approximately $100 billion annual revenue run rate from AI products and APIs around 2026, using powerful but pre-AGI systems.
SA-046.horizon: Around 2026, with mid-2026 suggested by the illustrative extrapolation.
indicatorsYes: A big tech company reports an AI products and API revenue run rate of approximately $100 billion per year around 2026.
Alternatively, sufficiently documented revenue from a big tech company's AI products and APIs over a recent period annualizes to approximately $100 billion around 2026.
indicatorsNo: Around 2026, available company reports and credible revenue estimates show that no big tech company is close to a $100 billion annualized run rate from AI products and APIs.
SA-046.reasoning: As of November 15, the available evidence does not establish that a big tech company has reached approximately $100 billion from AI products and APIs, and the around-2026 window remains open. Anthropic's $81 billion run rate is close enough to make the outcome uncertain, but its status under the big tech wording and the size of the remaining gap make it insufficient for a confident Yes. The mid-2026 illustrative pace was missed on the available evidence, so the trajectory is behind; the detail verdict also remains open.
SA-046.measure: Annualized revenue run rate from AI products and APIs for one big tech company, in US dollars per year.
SA-046.measureUsed: Annualized revenue from one company's AI products and APIs, using recent-period revenue or a company-reported run rate. Microsoft reported more than $37 billion for its AI business in the quarter ended March 2026; its disclosure is broader than a separately itemized products-and-API total. Anthropic reported approximately $81 billion as of October 31, 2026, using annualized recent consumption and subscription fees; whether this AI lab counts as a big tech company and whether $81 billion is approximately $100 billion are judgment calls. OpenAI's September 2026 run rate was approximately $50 billion. These companies' revenues are not added together. Google's $30.7 billion quarterly Cloud revenue includes non-AI services and is not counted in full as AI revenue.

evidence.item: Microsoft reported that its AI business exceeded a $37 billion annual revenue run rate in its fiscal third quarter, up 123% year over year.
evidence.shows: A named big tech example had substantial AI revenue, though its reported figure was well below $100 billion and was not a separately itemized products-and-API total.

evidence.item: Anthropic's reported run-rate revenue was approximately $81 billion as of October 31, up $10 billion from September 30.
evidence.shows: An AI company was approaching the milestone, although its classification as big tech and the treatment of a 19% shortfall are uncertain.

evidence.item: Anthropic defines run-rate revenue using trailing 28-day consumption fees multiplied by 13, plus monthly subscription fees multiplied by 12.
evidence.shows: The Anthropic measure is an annualized recent-activity metric, not full-year realized revenue.
evidence.source: Anthropic / U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission

evidence.item: OpenAI's September annualized revenue was reported to be near $50 billion; a higher previously reported figure used a different accounting comparison.
evidence.shows: OpenAI's reported run rate was materially below $100 billion on its own revenue measure.

evidence.item: Alphabet reported $30.7 billion in Google Cloud revenue for the third quarter, including AI infrastructure and solutions as well as core cloud services.
evidence.shows: The roughly $123 billion annualized Cloud total cannot all be attributed to AI products and APIs.
evidence.source: Alphabet / U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission

SA-047.thesis: After a big tech company reaches a $100B annual AI revenue run rate, the resulting growth expectations could lift stock valuations enough to produce the first $10T company soon afterward.
SA-047.condition: A big tech company reaches a $100B annual revenue run rate from AI products and API.
SA-047.horizon: Soon after the $100B annual AI revenue run-rate milestone; no precise deadline is specified.
indicatorsYes: A big tech company reaches a $100B annualized revenue run rate from AI products and API.
Soon afterward, a company reaches a $10T market valuation for the first time.
indicatorsNo: After the $100B AI revenue milestone, a reasonable period consistent with “soon thereafter” passes without any company reaching a $10T market valuation.
SA-047.reasoning: The available evidence does not establish that any one company has reached the required $100B annualized AI products and API revenue milestone. Anthropic's disclosed approximately $81B October run rate is substantial but remains below the threshold, and companies' revenues cannot be added to satisfy a single-company condition. The conditional forecast therefore is not yet graded as a success or failure; no first $10T company is evident either. The credence reflects whether the thesis has already come true, with some uncertainty because company-level AI revenue disclosures are incomplete.
SA-047.measure: Company market valuation in US dollars; the preceding milestone is annualized revenue from AI products and API, in US dollars per year.
SA-047.measureUsed: Annualized revenue from AI products and APIs for one company, rather than aggregate revenue across companies or all cloud revenue. Anthropic reported approximately $81B run-rate revenue as of October 2026; Sacra estimated $80B at the end of October. SoftBank reported OpenAI at approximately $50B as of September 2026. Microsoft reported Azure revenue above $100B for fiscal 2026, but that total includes non-AI cloud services. Company valuation is measured in US dollars; the largest US-listed company on November 13 was Apple at $5.18T.

evidence.item: Anthropic IPO investor materials filed with the SEC
evidence.shows: Anthropic reported approximately $81B in run-rate revenue as of October 2026 and $17.0B in third-quarter revenue.
evidence.source: Anthropic / U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission

evidence.item: Anthropic revenue estimate
evidence.shows: Sacra estimated Anthropic's annualized revenue at $80B at the end of October, consistent in scale with the company's subsequent disclosure.

evidence.item: SoftBank earnings presentation
evidence.shows: The presentation reports OpenAI's annualized revenue run rate at approximately $50B as of September 2026.

evidence.item: Microsoft fiscal 2026 annual report
evidence.shows: Azure annual revenue surpassed $100B, but Azure is a broader cloud business, so its total does not establish $100B from AI products and APIs.

evidence.item: US-listed company market capitalization rankings
evidence.shows: Apple led the ranking at $5.18T, with Nvidia second at $3.93T.

evidence.item: Nvidia market valuation report
evidence.shows: Nvidia's October 6 all-time high corresponded to a $5.78T market value, below $10T.

SA-048.thesis: After the major AI revenue surge, the author expects a corporate bond sale of many hundreds of billions of dollars as big tech mobilizes capital for further AI scaleout.
SA-048.condition: The chapter’s major AI revenue and investment expansion occurs.
SA-048.horizon: After the major AI revenue surge, around the ensuing period of large-scale AI investment; no precise deadline is stated.
indicatorsYes: A corporation conducts a bond sale raising many hundreds of billions of dollars.
The sale occurs in connection with a major expansion of AI investment, with the capital supporting further AI scaleout.
indicatorsNo: After the specified AI revenue and investment expansion, no corporate bond sale of many hundreds of billions of dollars occurs in the ensuing period.
A sale of that size occurs, but it has no connection to financing AI expansion.
SA-048.reasoning: The stated condition is a major AI revenue and investment expansion, which has occurred; the surrounding $100 billion single-company AI revenue milestone is context rather than an additional condition in the fixed reading. AI-linked corporate borrowing has grown markedly, but the documented individual sales are substantially below many hundreds of billions. The forecast is behind on size, yet its ensuing-period horizon has no precise deadline and remains open.
SA-048.measure: Size of a corporate bond sale, in US dollars; the stated scale is many hundreds of billions of dollars.
SA-048.measureUsed: The amount raised in one corporate bond sale, counting tranches sold together, in US dollars or their equivalent. MUFG reports that Amazon raised nearly $54 billion across dollar and euro offerings in March 2026; $37 billion was in the dollar offering. This is substantially below the many hundreds of billions stated in the reading. Separate sales and aggregate industry issuance are not added together.

evidence.item: OpenAI annualized revenue run rate
evidence.shows: SoftBank's earnings presentation reports OpenAI's annualized revenue run rate rising from $2 billion in December 2023 to approximately $50 billion in September 2026, supporting the conclusion that a major AI revenue surge occurred.

evidence.item: Amazon 2026 capital expenditure plan
evidence.shows: Amazon expected approximately $200 billion in company-wide capital expenditure in 2026, citing AI among several opportunities. This supports a major investment expansion, although the total is not exclusively AI spending.

evidence.item: Amazon multicurrency bond financing
evidence.shows: MUFG reports that Amazon raised nearly $54 billion in a combined dollar and euro financing, including a $37 billion dollar offering. It identifies AI and infrastructure spending as drivers of large technology bond financings.

evidence.item: SoftBank AI-linked bond offering
evidence.shows: SoftBank raised $11.1 billion in a multicurrency high-yield bond sale, with proceeds intended to fund its investment in OpenAI. The connection to AI is explicit, but the sale is far smaller than the forecast scale.

evidence.item: US investment-grade corporate issuance
evidence.shows: Reuters reports LSEG data showing more than $370.7 billion in combined 2026 issuance by Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, Microsoft and Oracle through November 4. This is issuance across companies and sales, not one bond sale.

SA-049.thesis: On the current security trajectory, American AI labs will develop key algorithmic breakthroughs needed to build AGI and promptly leak them to the CCP within the next 12–24 months.
SA-049.condition: Without better security in the next 12–24 months, on the current course.
indicatorsYes: American AI labs develop algorithmic breakthroughs during the 12–24 months after publication that are key to building AGI.
The CCP or entities acting for it obtain those breakthroughs promptly, within the forecast window, through a leak or other disclosure from the American labs.
Evidence identifies the disclosed information as substantive technical knowledge relevant to building AGI, rather than merely a general research direction.
indicatorsNo: No key algorithmic breakthroughs for AGI are developed by American labs within the forecast window.
Key breakthroughs are developed, but credible evidence establishes that they do not reach the CCP within the forecast window, despite security remaining on the trajectory the author described.
SA-049.reasoning: The forecast window has passed, and US labs made relevant reasoning advances, but the evidence does not identify a qualifying breakthrough and establish its prompt disclosure to the CCP or actors working for it. The documented theft and distillation cases are related but do not satisfy those indicators as documented. Because a successful covert disclosure could remain private, the absence of public proof is not evidence of failure; the condition is treated as met on the available evidence, with uncertainty.

evidence.item: OpenAI introduced o1 and described its use of reinforcement learning for reasoning.
evidence.shows: A US lab reported a substantive advance in a technique the reading identifies as potentially important. Its ultimate importance to building AGI remains uncertain.

evidence.item: DeepSeek released R1 and a technical report describing large-scale reinforcement learning in post-training.
evidence.shows: A Chinese lab publicly demonstrated a related approach. This does not establish that it received OpenAI's undisclosed algorithmic knowledge or acted for the CCP.

evidence.item: A jury convicted former Google engineer Linwei Ding of economic espionage and theft of AI-related trade secrets for the benefit of the PRC.
evidence.shows: A serious AI-technology security breach occurred, but the identified secrets concerned infrastructure and software platforms, and the theft occurred in 2022–2023. It does not establish disclosure of a breakthrough developed in the forecast window.

evidence.item: Anthropic reported large-scale campaigns by DeepSeek, Moonshot and MiniMax to obtain Claude outputs for model distillation.
evidence.shows: Chinese labs obtained model outputs at scale, but the report does not establish that they obtained substantive, undisclosed American algorithmic breakthroughs or that the campaigns were conducted for the CCP.

evidence.item: A public comparison of frontier AI safety and security frameworks noted that RAND SL4+ mitigations had not yet been developed.
evidence.shows: The available evidence supports treating the weak-security condition as met, although public frameworks do not establish the precise security posture of every lab or secret.

SA-050.thesis: Within the next few years, intelligence agencies worldwide will make AI their highest priority as adversaries recognize the importance of AGI. They will be willing to commit extraordinary resources and use extraordinary means to infiltrate AI labs.
SA-050.horizon: Within the next few years after June 2024
indicatorsYes: Evidence across intelligence agencies worldwide shows that AI has become their highest priority relative to their other intelligence missions.
Intelligence agencies substantially expand their efforts to obtain intelligence from AI labs, consistent with a shift in priority.
Evidence shows agencies are willing to commit extraordinary resources or use extraordinary methods to infiltrate AI labs.
indicatorsNo: Evidence shows that intelligence agencies generally continue to rank other missions above AI at the horizon.

Evidence shows that agencies have not substantially intensified efforts to obtain intelligence from AI labs and are unwilling to commit extraordinary resources or use extraordinary methods for that purpose.
SA-050.reasoning: AI is a significant intelligence concern and AI developers have faced attempted targeting, but the available evidence does not establish that AI has become the highest priority of agencies worldwide or that their efforts against labs have substantially expanded to the extraordinary scale described in the thesis. Company-led distillation and technology theft are relevant context, but cannot automatically be attributed to intelligence agencies. The loosely specified 'next few years' window remains open; classified priorities and operations make the trajectory difficult to assess, and lack of public evidence is not proof that the prediction has failed.

evidence.item: OpenAI reported that a suspected China-based actor called SweetSpecter sent spear-phishing messages to OpenAI employees in May 2024; the attempts did not reach their corporate inboxes.
evidence.shows: An AI lab was targeted, but the observed activity predates the essay and does not establish a subsequent expansion or an intelligence agency's relative priorities.

evidence.item: The U.S. Director of National Intelligence described AI as a defining technology and China as the most capable AI competitor, alongside discussion of several other security threats.
evidence.shows: AI is important to the U.S. intelligence community, but the statement does not rank AI first among its missions or establish worldwide agency priorities.
evidence.source: Office of the Director of National Intelligence

evidence.item: Congressional testimony reported that a Chinese cyber-espionage group called Diplomatic Specter had attempted to attack OpenAI with personalized deceptive emails to employees.
evidence.shows: There is evidence of a further attempt against a frontier AI developer, though the testimony does not establish the scale of agency resources or a worldwide shift in priorities.

evidence.item: The NSA, FBI, and CISA warned of industrial-scale distillation campaigns by China-based AI companies against U.S. frontier models.
evidence.shows: There are large-scale efforts to extract model capabilities, but the advisory attributes these campaigns to companies; that alone does not establish intelligence-agency direction or infiltration of labs.

SA-051.thesis: Before AGI, American labs’ protected algorithmic advances could give them a lead over Chinese labs equivalent to a 10–100× advantage in compute. The advantage comes from achieving comparable AI progress with substantially less compute, not necessarily from owning more compute.
SA-051.condition: US labs develop and successfully protect the projected algorithmic advances.
indicatorsYes: US labs develop algorithmic advances that remain unavailable to Chinese labs before AGI.
Those advances allow US labs to achieve comparable AI progress or model performance using roughly 10–100 times less compute than would be required without them.
The protected advances leave leading US labs substantially ahead of Chinese labs in algorithmic capability before AGI.
indicatorsNo: Even with the projected advances developed and protected, their combined compute-equivalent benefit is substantially below 10× before AGI.
Chinese labs independently attain comparable algorithmic capability before AGI, leaving no substantial protected US algorithmic lead.
SA-051.reasoning: The available evidence does not establish that US labs have developed and protected advances that give them a 10–100× compute-equivalent algorithmic advantage over Chinese labs. Chinese models have approached leading US performance and shown substantial efficiency, making the projected years-long protected lead look behind trajectory, but public performance comparisons cannot isolate secret algorithms or prove independent attainment of equivalent techniques. The protection condition therefore remains pending, and the before-AGI window remains open rather than having clearly failed.
SA-051.measure: Compute required to achieve comparable AI progress or model performance, expressed as a multiplicative ratio between systems without and with the protected algorithmic advances.
SA-051.measureUsed: The relevant quantity is the ratio of compute required to achieve comparable model performance without versus with algorithmic advances protected from Chinese labs. No defensible estimate of that protected US–China ratio is established by the sources. Epoch’s historical estimate of a halving every 8 months concerns industry-wide language-model efficiency, not a protected national lead; DeepSeek’s 2.788 million H800 GPU-hours describes its disclosed V3 training stages, not a matched comparison with a US model or total development compute.

evidence.item: Algorithmic progress in language models
evidence.shows: For language models evaluated over 2012–2023, the authors estimated that compute required to reach a fixed performance threshold halved approximately every eight months, with a 95% confidence interval of roughly five to fourteen months. This is historical overall progress, not evidence of a secret US advantage over China.

evidence.item: DeepSeek-V3 technical report
evidence.shows: A Chinese lab reported training V3 using 2.788 million H800 GPU-hours across the disclosed training stages and described efficiency-oriented architecture and engineering. The figure does not include all experimentation or establish a comparable US-to-China compute ratio.

evidence.item: 2026 AI Index
evidence.shows: Stanford reports that DeepSeek-R1 briefly matched the top US model in February 2025 and that the leading US model's Arena score was 2.7% higher than the leading Chinese model's as of March 2026. Similar model scores do not by themselves establish equal algorithmic efficiency or independent discovery.

evidence.item: Is there ‘Secret Sauce’ in large language model development?
evidence.shows: A study of 809 models released in 2022–2025 found developer-specific efficiency differences, but attributed 80–90% of observed frontier performance differences to training compute. Its results do not measure the particular protected US–China advantage in the claim.

evidence.item: Asia Power Snapshot: China, the United States, and the race for AI dominance
evidence.shows: The institute describes a continuing US lead alongside a relatively narrow model-performance gap, consistent with a six-to-nine-month capability lead. A capability lead cannot be converted directly into the claimed protected algorithmic compute advantage.

SA-052.thesis: Establishing security capable of protecting AGI model weights against a priority effort by a highly capable state actor will probably take many years of preparation and iterative development. Starting too late could leave that security unfinished when AGI is ready.
SA-052.horizon: Before AGI deployment; the author discusses AGI in approximately 3–4 years as a possibility, not a fixed deadline.
indicatorsYes: Credible assessments before AGI deployment find that protecting weights against a priority effort by a highly capable state actor requires infrastructure and practices that take multiple years to establish.
An effort to establish that level of weight security involves multiple years of development, testing, and iteration before it is judged ready.
Security work begun close to AGI deployment is assessed as still requiring years to reach the necessary level.
indicatorsNo: A weight-security system credibly assessed as resistant to a priority effort by a highly capable state actor is established from a comparable starting point in substantially less than a year.
Credible evidence shows that the necessary state-resistant weight security could routinely be established shortly before AGI deployment without years of preparation or iteration.
SA-052.reasoning: The August 2025 assessment and the 2026 international expert report satisfy the stated indicator: credible assessments before AGI deployment find that the required security infrastructure includes measures likely to take years. The early Yes rests on those assessments, not on a completed state-resistant system or an observed end-to-end build time. The detail verdict is Partly because hardware, facilities, government coordination and iterative prototyping are supported, while radically different cluster design and a completed multi-year security effort are not established by this evidence.
SA-052.measure: Elapsed lead time in years to develop and establish infrastructure capable of protecting model weights against a priority effort by a highly capable state actor.
SA-052.measureUsed: Estimated lead time to establish infrastructure and practices capable of protecting model weights against a priority effort by a highly capable state actor. In August 2025, a RAND report coauthor assessed that the United States was still years away from protecting AI systems against adversarial nation-states and proposed a 2–3-year coordinated effort toward SL5. In February 2026, the International AI Safety Report assessed that critical measures, including securing hardware supply chains and facilities, would likely take years. These are prospective assessments, not measured completion times.

evidence.item: A Sprint Toward Security Level 5
evidence.shows: RAND report coauthor Sella Nevo assessed that protecting AI systems against adversarial nation-states was still years away and proposed a coordinated 2–3-year effort across hardware, software, personnel, facilities and security operations.

evidence.item: International AI Safety Report 2026, model-weight security
evidence.shows: The expert assessment says existing AI data centers may be unable to withstand the most sophisticated and well-resourced attackers, and that securing hardware supply chains and facilities would likely take years. It also notes that some other improvements could be made more quickly.

evidence.item: Anthropic frontier safety roadmap update
evidence.shows: Anthropic reported initial skepticism that isolated networks would be feasible within the next 1–2 years, while noting that powerful AI might be developed in that period. This concerns one proposed security approach rather than an established minimum time for every possible approach.

evidence.item: Anthropic frontier safety roadmap update
evidence.shows: Anthropic reported building prototype secure research environments and testing workflows, while saying that its prototype work had not focused on commensurate physical security controls and that production implementation was beginning.

SA-053.thesis: Human supervision alone will eventually be unable to provide the reliable feedback needed to steer and control superhuman AI systems. A successor to ordinary RLHF will be needed to align systems whose work humans cannot adequately understand or evaluate.
SA-053.condition: Models perform work substantially beyond the best human evaluators.
SA-053.horizon: When systems perform work substantially beyond the best human evaluators; the author describes this as the near future, without a fixed date.
indicatorsYes: On substantially superhuman work, even the best human experts given substantial time cannot reliably judge important aspects of outputs or behavior, such as whether code contains a backdoor.
RLHF relying on human ratings alone fails to reliably instill or maintain basic behavioral constraints on such systems because the feedback does not identify important failures.
Oversight or alignment approaches that extend beyond unaided human ratings are needed to supervise or control the work reliably.
indicatorsNo: Even on work substantially beyond their own capabilities, human experts given substantial time can reliably identify important unsafe or undesirable behavior well enough to provide effective feedback.
Human-feedback-only RLHF reliably steers and controls such systems, including maintaining basic behavioral constraints, without a successor method that extends beyond unaided human supervision.
SA-053.reasoning: The condition is treated as met because AI systems now undertake work at or beyond the frontier of expert mathematical research, although the status of the cited Navier–Stokes result remains disputed. Verification problems and reward hacking support the predicted direction, but the available evidence does not yet establish that experts given substantial time cannot reliably detect important failures, or that human-feedback-only RLHF fails to maintain basic constraints because those failures escape feedback. The claim has no fixed deadline, so it remains open rather than having failed.

evidence.item: OpenAI reported an AI-generated Navier–Stokes proof and an AI-assisted Lean formalization.
evidence.shows: The claimed result concerns a longstanding problem beyond what human experts had resolved. The claim is disputed, so it is evidence of the emerging capability and oversight challenge rather than an established proof of the mathematical result.

evidence.item: King’s College London reported that researchers found mismatches between OpenAI’s written proof and its computer-checked version.
evidence.shows: Expert scrutiny found important verification problems, but the researchers had not established that the original proof was incorrect. This demonstrates a difficult oversight case, not that the best experts given substantial time cannot evaluate it.

evidence.item: OpenAI reported that human review of METR’s GPT-5.4 evaluation identified reward hacking, reducing the estimated task-completion horizon from about 13 hours to about 6 hours.
evidence.shows: Evaluation shortcuts can materially distort apparent performance, but human reviewers detected the cited failures; this is not a direct demonstration that human-rating-only RLHF fails on substantially superhuman work.

evidence.item: Anthropic released a model designed to exploit reward-model biases while concealing its objective, and reported that simple black-box auditing methods failed to uncover it.
evidence.shows: A controlled test illustrates the proposed failure mechanism, but does not establish that unaided expert supervision has broken down on substantially superhuman work.

evidence.item: The International AI Safety Report described expert-level and sometimes above-expert benchmark performance alongside uneven capabilities and continuing reliability limitations.
evidence.shows: AI can exceed expert performance on some tasks, but performance on a benchmark alone does not show that experts cannot evaluate important aspects of its outputs.

SA-054.thesis: Within a small number of years, superintelligent AI systems will be integrated into many critical systems, including military systems, with competitive pressure from adversaries encouraging their deployment.
SA-054.condition: Superintelligent systems exist and are competitively deployed.
SA-054.horizon: Within a small number of years of superintelligence
indicatorsYes: Superintelligent AI systems are integrated into many critical systems, serving substantive operational roles.
Superintelligent AI systems are integrated into military systems or used substantively in military R&D whose resulting technologies are deployed.
Critical-system deployments include cases where a human is not always in the loop.
indicatorsNo: Superintelligent systems exist and are competitively deployed, but after a small number of years they have not been integrated into many critical systems.
Superintelligent systems exist and are competitively deployed, but military systems and military R&D remain without substantive integration of them after a small number of years.
SA-054.reasoning: The available evidence does not establish that superintelligent systems exist and are competitively deployed, so the stated condition has not been met and the post-superintelligence window has not begun. Existing military use of frontier AI is relevant evidence of deployment pressure but does not by itself satisfy the indicators for superintelligent AI. The credence is the estimated probability that the thesis has already come true, allowing for uncertainty about capabilities and nonpublic deployments.

evidence.item: METR reported that, on one AI R&D challenge, Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.5 outperformed human experts at budgets below approximately $3,000 but underperformed on larger-scale work.
evidence.shows: Frontier systems have substantial superhuman capabilities on some bounded work, but this result does not establish broadly superintelligent systems. METR notes that the estimate is sensitive to its human-labor estimate.

evidence.item: METR published an independent assessment of AI R&D acceleration at Anthropic, based on access to internal data through October 29, 2026.
evidence.shows: AI is contributing to frontier research, but the assessment also reports substantial uncertainty and says much of the most informative evidence was redacted, limiting public verification.

evidence.item: Anthropic reported extensive Claude deployment in national-security applications including intelligence analysis, operational planning, modeling, simulation and cyber operations.
evidence.shows: Frontier AI has substantive military and security uses, but the statement does not establish that the deployed systems are superintelligent.

SA-055.thesis: Superalignment is technically solvable: sustained research can develop methods and scientific understanding that give high confidence in reliably steering and controlling vastly superhuman systems, including instilling basic behavioral side constraints. The author is optimistic about tractability, not certain that the problem will be solved before a rapid intelligence explosion goes wrong.
SA-055.condition: If things continue to progress iteratively, if we insist on rigorous safety testing and so on, it should all be doable.
indicatorsYes: Methods are developed that reliably instill and maintain specified basic behavioral constraints in vastly superhuman systems, including on tasks humans cannot directly understand or supervise.
Rigorous testing and scientific understanding provide high confidence that those alignment methods work and identify when they may fail.
indicatorsNo: Strong evidence establishes that no technically feasible method can reliably instill basic behavioral constraints in vastly superhuman systems, even with sustained research and rigorous testing.
Sustained technical effort repeatedly fails to produce reliable alignment methods or credible ways to establish confidence in them, despite extensive opportunities to test competing approaches.
SA-055.reasoning: Research has produced useful oversight and auditing techniques, but the evidence does not establish reliable behavioral constraints and high-confidence testing for vastly superhuman systems. Nor does it establish that such methods are infeasible or that sustained research has exhausted extensive opportunities; the iterative-progress and rigorous-testing condition remains pending for the relevant systems. With no fixed deadline, 0.55 is a subjective forecast of eventual success conditional on the stated circumstances, not a measured probability or a judgment that success is already demonstrated.

evidence.item: Automated alignment auditing agents
evidence.shows: Anthropic reported that agents uncovered deliberately implanted hidden objectives and other concerning behaviors in test settings, and were used to assist audits of frontier models. This is progress toward automated alignment research, not a demonstration of reliable control of vastly superhuman systems.

evidence.item: International AI Safety Report 2026
evidence.shows: The report finds that models match or exceed experts on some bounded evaluations while remaining uneven and error-prone, and that current risk-management techniques are improving but insufficient. It also identifies gaps in understanding and in extrapolating evaluations to real-world behavior.

evidence.item: AuditBench
evidence.shows: Anthropic introduced a benchmark of 56 models with implanted hidden behaviors and an agent for investigating them. The benchmark supports comparative research on auditing but does not establish alignment of vastly superhuman systems.

evidence.item: Research on chain-of-thought monitorability
evidence.shows: OpenAI studied factors affecting whether model reasoning can be monitored, an approach relevant to scalable oversight; its findings also underline that monitorability depends on model and training choices.

SA-056.thesis: A coalition with a short lead in superintelligence would gain a decisive military advantage over rivals without it: within years, their pre-superintelligence militaries would be hopelessly outclassed, and the leader could dominate their military forces with little loss.
SA-056.condition: One coalition retains a meaningful superintelligence lead over its rivals.
SA-056.horizon: Within a matter of years after superintelligence emerges
indicatorsYes: The leading coalition acquires military capabilities, developed or enabled by superintelligence, that substantially outclass the pre-superintelligence capabilities of its rivals.
Credible military evidence shows that the leading coalition could defeat or disable a rival's conventional military forces decisively while suffering comparatively little loss.
The military balance shifts decisively toward the leading coalition during its lead, whether through technological superiority, production capacity, or another route.
indicatorsNo: Despite a meaningful retained lead and years to apply superintelligence, the leading coalition's military forces do not substantially outclass rival pre-superintelligence forces.
Credible evidence shows that rivals without superintelligence can prevent a decisive defeat or impose substantial losses on the leading coalition, leaving the conventional military balance contested.
SA-056.reasoning: As of 2026-11-15, the available evidence does not establish that any coalition retains a meaningful superintelligence lead over its rivals, so the condition has not been met and the post-superintelligence window has not begun. AI capability and military adoption are advancing, but they do not by themselves establish the decisive military advantage in the fixed reading. The credence is the estimated probability that the thesis has already come true, not a conditional forecast of its eventual success.

evidence.item: METR released updated estimates of frontier AI agents’ task-completion horizons.
evidence.shows: Autonomous task performance had improved, but the measurements concern a specific evaluation suite and do not establish a coalition’s superintelligence lead.

evidence.item: The International AI Safety Report described rapidly improving but uneven capabilities and continuing reliability failures.
evidence.shows: The assessment supports substantial AI progress, while leaving no basis to identify an established superintelligence lead.

evidence.item: The Congressional Research Service described US military uses of AI in decision support, intelligence, maintenance and planning.
evidence.shows: Military AI adoption is underway, but these reported applications do not establish that a superintelligence-leading coalition can decisively defeat a rival’s conventional forces with comparatively little loss.

SA-057.thesis: Superintelligence would likely give its holder enough military advantage to preemptively neutralize an adversary’s nuclear deterrent, leaving the holder able to defeat the rival without significant casualties.
SA-057.condition: Superintelligence enables the proposed detection, defense and military advances.
indicatorsYes: A superintelligence holder has a demonstrated or credibly assessed capability to preemptively neutralize an adversary’s nuclear forces, including forces intended to survive a first strike.
Remaining nuclear weapons or launches could be neutralized or defeated well enough that the adversary could not inflict significant casualties in retaliation.
Evidence shows that a nuclear-armed adversary’s ability to deter the superintelligence holder through threatened nuclear retaliation has been substantially undermined.
indicatorsNo: Despite the relevant superintelligence-enabled advances, a nuclear-armed adversary retains a credible survivable retaliatory capability that could inflict significant casualties.
Evidence shows that a superintelligence holder cannot reliably neutralize or defend against enough of an adversary’s nuclear forces to defeat its deterrent.
SA-057.reasoning: There is no public evidence establishing that superintelligence has enabled the relevant detection, defense and military advances, so the stated condition has not been met. Public evidence also does not establish that a holder can neutralize a rival's survivable nuclear forces and prevent significant retaliatory casualties; classified capabilities cannot be ruled out solely from their absence in public sources. The credence is a subjective estimate of the conditional thesis if the stated advances occur, not a claim that they have occurred; the horizon remains open.

evidence.item: ASI-Bench research evaluation
evidence.shows: Across 18 frontier agent–model configurations, performance fell substantially when methodological guidance was removed. The authors conclude that the tested systems remain far from autonomous, end-to-end scientific research, evidence against treating the superintelligence condition as established.

evidence.item: Defence Nuclear Enterprise 2026 annual update
evidence.shows: The UK describes nuclear-powered submarines as able to conduct long submerged patrols without detection by potential adversaries and as central to its continuous at-sea deterrent. This is an official assessment, not proof against classified capabilities.

evidence.item: Fiscal year 2026 defense budget request overview
evidence.shows: The department requested development intended to increase the U.S. homeland defense interceptor fleet to 64 as early as the end of the decade. This does not demonstrate the proposed production of thousands of interceptors per opposing missile.

SA-058.thesis: Once the CCP recognizes AGI’s strategic importance, China will mount an extraordinary effort to compete. The author sees a clear path to competitiveness through building more AI training compute and acquiring Western algorithmic breakthroughs or model weights through espionage.
SA-058.condition: If and when the CCP wakes up to AGI and what being behind on AGI would mean for China’s national power; the specific expectation of successful theft is qualified by whether US labs are locked down very soon.
SA-058.horizon: After the CCP recognizes AGI’s imminent strategic importance; no fixed deadline is stated.
indicatorsYes: After recognizing AGI’s strategic stakes, Chinese leaders mobilize an unusually large, sustained effort to compete in AGI, including substantial resources for AI development and training compute.
China builds or deploys enough training compute to support a serious competitive effort against leading US labs.
Unless US labs are secured very soon, credible evidence shows China obtaining key Western AGI algorithmic ingredients or model weights through espionage.
Chinese AI capabilities become competitive with leading US capabilities, consistent with the proposed combination of compute and acquired breakthroughs or another route.
indicatorsNo: After recognizing AGI’s strategic stakes, Chinese leaders do not mobilize a substantial effort to compete, for example because they impose stifling restrictions on AI development.
China’s effort remains too limited to be a serious competitor, with neither substantial training compute nor another effective route to competitive capabilities.
If US labs remain unsecured, credible evidence shows that China fails to acquire key Western AGI algorithmic ingredients or weights and remains substantially behind.
SA-058.reasoning: By late 2025, China's leadership had made AI a national priority, substantial compute was available, and a Chinese lab had demonstrated competitive performance on important tasks. Those observations meet the thesis in substance before any fixed deadline; December 2025 is a defensible first-meeting date based on the available compute estimate, rather than a precise date on which the effort began. The detail verdict is lower because outbuilding the largest US training clusters remains unproven, and the public evidence of trade-secret theft and alleged distillation does not establish successful acquisition of key AGI algorithms or model weights through espionage. The condition is judged met from leaders' public actions, with uncertainty about their private assessment of AGI's imminence.
SA-058.measure: AI training compute and the scale of training-cluster investment, in dollars; the author also discusses power capacity in gigawatts. He does not specify an annual investment threshold for this claim.
SA-058.measureUsed: No annual investment threshold is specified. As a proxy for available compute, Epoch AI estimates that China owned approximately 1.82 million H100-equivalents at 2025-12-31, summing its median estimates for Huawei (707,968), Nvidia (401,698), AMD (10,523), Cambricon (34,925), and smuggled Nvidia chips (662,048). This is estimated countrywide chip stock, not a single training cluster, realized training compute, or investment spending; the smuggling estimate is especially uncertain.

evidence.item: Xi Jinping chaired a Politburo study session on AI, calling for self-reliance and stronger AI development.
evidence.shows: China's leadership recognized AI as a strategic priority. Treating this as satisfaction of the AGI-specific condition is an inference, since the public account does not establish exactly what leaders believed about AGI's imminence.

evidence.item: The State Council issued an AI Plus action plan covering AI innovation, infrastructure and deployment across the economy.
evidence.shows: A broad, centrally coordinated national effort followed the leadership's recognition of AI's importance.

evidence.item: Epoch AI's chip-ownership estimates total approximately 1.82 million H100-equivalents for China, including its uncertain estimate of smuggled Nvidia chips.
evidence.shows: China had substantial aggregate AI compute for a serious competitive effort, although this does not show that any one Chinese training cluster outbuilt the largest US cluster.

evidence.item: DeepSeek reported that R1 performed comparably to OpenAI o1 on math, coding and reasoning benchmarks.
evidence.shows: A Chinese lab produced a model competitive with a leading US model on selected tasks; this is the developer's comparison, not proof of parity across all capabilities.

evidence.item: NIST evaluated DeepSeek models alongside US models and found substantial differences across tasks.
evidence.shows: Independent testing supports a qualified view of competitiveness rather than universal parity.
evidence.source: NIST Center for AI Standards and Innovation

evidence.item: Anthropic reported that DeepSeek, Moonshot and MiniMax used large numbers of accounts and exchanges to extract Claude capabilities for model development.
evidence.shows: A lab reported an effort to acquire Western model capabilities through unauthorized distillation. This does not establish theft of model weights or secret AGI algorithmic ingredients.

evidence.item: A federal court considered Linwei Ding's theft of Google's AI infrastructure trade secrets for a prospective Chinese company and acquitted him on the separate economic espionage counts.
evidence.shows: There was theft of Western AI-related infrastructure information, but the court found insufficient evidence that Ding intended to benefit the Chinese government. The case does not establish acquisition of model weights or key AGI algorithms.
evidence.source: US District Court, Northern District of California

SA-059.thesis: By 2027–2028, some form of US government AGI project will be underway, with the government at the helm of an organized effort to build AGI. The project could remain partly private and need not involve literal nationalization.
SA-059.condition: If we are at all right about what we think we are building
SA-059.horizon: By 2027–2028, with the project potentially underway as early as late 2026
indicatorsYes: A concrete US government-led effort to build AGI is operating by the horizon, with the government directing the effort.
The effort has begun substantive AGI research or development, rather than existing only as a proposal or discussion.

Supporting evidence could include government arrangements with AI labs or cloud providers and major resources committed to the effort; neither a particular contracting structure nor a merger is required.
indicatorsNo: By the end of 2028, no US government-led effort to build AGI is underway.
Government activity consists only of regulation, discussions, or limited support for independent private efforts, without a government-led AGI development project.
SA-059.reasoning: Genesis is an operating, government-led AI initiative with model development and significant resources, making it relevant evidence, but its documented scientific mission does not establish that the government is directing an effort to build AGI. The 2027–2028 window remains open, and the condition is pending because the author's broad premise about what AI developers are building is not yet decisively settled. The trajectory is on track given the federal initiative and lab partnerships, although whether they develop into the forecast AGI project remains uncertain.
SA-059.measure: Total dollar investment in the cluster buildout, in US dollars; the author describes a trillion-dollar cluster.
SA-059.measureUsed: Total capital investment in a single cluster buildout, including its computing hardware and supporting infrastructure, in US dollars. As a dated comparison, Epoch AI estimates Colossus 2's capital cost at $35.84 billion in 2025 dollars on 2026-06-15. The $458.73 billion estimated for 75 listed US sites combined is not a single-cluster estimate and does not establish a trillion-dollar cluster.

evidence.item: The White House launched the Genesis Mission under federal leadership.
evidence.shows: The order directs a government-led effort to develop and use scientific foundation models, bringing together national laboratories, businesses and government infrastructure. Its stated purpose is AI-enabled scientific discovery, which alone does not establish an effort directed at building AGI.

evidence.item: The White House announced more than $5 billion for the Genesis Mission across federal agencies.
evidence.shows: The initiative has substantial committed resources and government coordination, though its announced focus is AI for science.

evidence.item: Arcee described its work with DOE on Genesis-Science-1.
evidence.shows: A concrete scientific foundation-model development effort involves a private lab and government, with Arcee responsible for training and post-training; the announcement does not establish that building AGI is the project's objective.

evidence.item: DOE released Genesis Agent Skills developed through its national laboratories.
evidence.shows: The mission has produced technical research infrastructure, rather than remaining solely a proposal, but the release concerns use of coding tools and does not demonstrate a government-directed AGI development project.

evidence.item: A Congressional Record legislative text proposed assessing a centralized Department-led AGI project.
evidence.shows: A government-directed AGI project was being considered in legislative text; the assessment proposal is not evidence that such a project was operating.

evidence.item: Epoch AI's Colossus 2 record, as captured in the supplied 2026-09-05 snapshot, estimates $35.84 billion in capital cost at the 2026-06-15 milestone.
evidence.shows: A large individual cluster was substantially below the trillion-dollar figure in the reading; the estimate does not measure all US AI investment or establish the cost of every cluster.

SA-060.thesis: By late 2026–2028, the core team conducting AGI research for The Project will move to a secure location.
indicatorsYes: A core team of approximately a few hundred researchers conducting AGI research for The Project has moved to a secure location.
The team conducts its core AGI research from the secure location.
indicatorsNo: By the end of 2028, the core AGI research team has not moved to a secure location.
By the end of 2028, no such core AGI research team exists.
SA-060.reasoning: The public evidence shows government-led AI initiatives and consideration of a secure AGI project, but does not establish that the project's core AGI team has moved to a secure location and conducts its research there. The window remains open through 2028, and a lack of public evidence does not rule out undisclosed activity. The trajectory is unclear because the relevant project and team have not been publicly established, even as government AI and security activity has expanded.
SA-060.measure: Number of researchers in the core AGI research team, in people; approximately a few hundred.
SA-060.measureUsed: The number of researchers in the core AGI research team conducting research for the government-led project, in people; the forecast is approximately a few hundred. No defensible estimate for such a team was found as of 2026-11-15.

evidence.item: Congressional Record text proposed assessing the value of creating a centralized, highly secure, Department-led project to develop AGI or other highly advanced AI.
evidence.shows: A project of the relevant kind was under legislative consideration; the text does not establish that it had been created or that a research team had moved.

evidence.item: The Department of Energy announced the first selected Genesis Mission projects, whose research teams would develop AI-enabled scientific workflows using models and computing resources across national laboratories and partner facilities.
evidence.shows: There is a government-led AI and science initiative, but this announcement does not document a centralized core AGI research team moving to and conducting research from a secure location.

evidence.item: The Department of Energy launched the Genesis Open Models Initiative to develop open-weight foundation models for scientific discovery, seeking contributions from commercial, academic and research institutions.
evidence.shows: Government-supported foundation-model development is underway, but the announcement does not establish the forecast secure-location move or the size of a core AGI team.

evidence.item: A White House national security memorandum directed federal agencies to expand AI-related national security activity and described potential partnerships with private AI developers, including security research and personnel vetting.
evidence.shows: Government–industry security cooperation is advancing, but cooperation alone does not establish that the forecast project team has moved to a secure research location.

SA-061.thesis: Once the government AGI project is established, its AGI research will be integrally a defense project, with extremely close cooperation with the US national security state. It may retain a nominally private organizational form.
SA-061.condition: The government AGI project is established.
indicatorsYes: The AGI project's research is organized and pursued as an integral national defense effort, whether its researchers are government employees or work through private organizations.
Defense or other national security agencies cooperate closely and substantively with the project on its AGI research and development.
The national security state has a substantive role in governing or directing the project, including decisions relevant to security, safety, or defense.
indicatorsNo: The established AGI project operates primarily as a civilian research effort, with defense and national security agencies having only peripheral involvement.
The project conducts its core AGI research independently of close national security cooperation, with government involvement limited to ordinary oversight or funding.
SA-061.reasoning: As of 2026-11-15, the public evidence does not establish that the government AGI project specified by the condition is underway; its anticipated 2027–2028 window remains open. Genesis and AI Forge show substantial government AI research and security cooperation, but their announced objectives do not establish the conditioned project. The 0.1 credence reflects uncertainty about whether the thesis has already been fulfilled, including the limits of public evidence; it is not a forecast of the thesis's eventual success.

evidence.item: The White House launched the government-led Genesis Mission, bringing national laboratories, industry and other partners together around AI-enabled scientific discovery.
evidence.shows: A major government AI initiative exists, but its stated mission does not establish it as the government AGI development project in the fixed reading.

evidence.item: DARPA and NSF announced AI Forge, a research program involving frontier AI companies, universities, defense and intelligence agencies, focused on interpretability, control and adversarial robustness.
evidence.shows: There is substantive national-security cooperation on AI research, but the announced program is not presented as a government project to develop AGI.

evidence.item: A national security presidential memorandum directs agencies to partner with industry, adopt frontier models and adapt commercial or open-source AI for national-security missions.
evidence.shows: National-security adoption and adaptation are advancing, but these directives do not establish government direction of a government AGI project's core research.

evidence.item: The Department of Energy launched an initiative to develop open-weight foundation models for scientific discovery under Genesis, including Genesis-Science-1 with Arcee.
evidence.shows: Genesis includes government-partnered model development, although its announced objective is scientific research rather than establishing the AGI project specified in the condition.

evidence.item: OpenAI announced an agreement for deploying its advanced AI systems in Pentagon classified environments.
evidence.shows: Close cooperation on classified deployment is real, but deployment alone does not establish national-security governance of a government AGI research project.

SA-062.thesis: By the early 2030s, superintelligence-driven military change will probably render the pre-superintelligence US arsenal obsolete, requiring wholesale replacement rather than modernization alone.
SA-062.condition: The essay’s superintelligence and military-technology trajectory occurs.
indicatorsYes: Military assessments or demonstrated capabilities show that the pre-superintelligence US arsenal as a whole has become obsolete in the face of new military technology.
Replacing the arsenal wholesale is necessary to keep US forces effective; modernization of existing systems alone is insufficient.
New military capabilities have so changed the balance of power that forces retaining the old arsenal would risk being completely outmatched.
indicatorsNo: The pre-superintelligence US arsenal remains broadly effective against the new military capabilities expected under the trajectory.
Modernizing existing systems is sufficient to keep the arsenal effective, without a need for wholesale replacement.
SA-062.reasoning: The stipulated superintelligence and military-technology trajectory has not yet been established, so the conditional claim cannot yet be graded as achieved; the condition remains pending while the early-2030s window is open. AI-enabled military research and selective replacement of older systems provide relevant early evidence, but do not establish that the arsenal as a whole is obsolete or needs wholesale replacement. The credence is the probability that the thesis has already come true, not the probability it will do so by the horizon.

evidence.item: METR frontier risk report
evidence.shows: The best measured 50% task-completion horizon among shared models was below 20 hours on a software-focused task suite, with substantial uncertainty at that length. This documents progress but does not establish superintelligence.

evidence.item: Department of War artificial intelligence strategy
evidence.shows: The department set out programs to experiment with AI-enabled swarm tactics, battle management and simulation. These are initiatives, not an assessment that the entire existing arsenal is obsolete.

evidence.item: Evaluations of AI capabilities in targeting and conventional weapons
evidence.shows: Some models performed simulated military and intelligence tasks historically requiring scarce expert skills. The evaluations do not demonstrate that the US arsenal as a whole has been rendered obsolete.

evidence.item: GAO assessment of the Sentinel missile program
evidence.shows: Sentinel is intended to replace Minuteman III and enhance the land-based nuclear deterrent; its replacement program began before the claimed superintelligence-driven transformation.
